days.movement: No cycling -- full morning off the bike, it's Saturday and this is the week's long run. U-Bahn to the start if needed.
days.food: Carb-focused dinner Friday night, solid pre-run breakfast, and a gel if the run runs past ~60 minutes. Recovery meal with protein within 30 min of finishing.
days.bigPicture: Week 7's closing long run -- 105 minutes (~18km), the biggest single session of the week and a step up from last week's 17.4km. Comes after both of this week's quality days, so it's the real test of whether the new two-quality-day structure is absorbing cleanly.

training.title: Sunday easy run (short)
training.detail: 15 min very easy (~65-75% LT) — recovery week, kept short rather than skipped, same as the other recovery-week sessions

days.movement: No commute today, it's the weekend -- a short recovery-week shakeout only, nothing to plan around.
days.food: Normal balanced meals -- this is a deliberately light day, not a fueling day.
days.bigPicture: First day of week 8, a recovery week -- kept to a short 15-minute shakeout rather than skipped entirely, same pattern as the plan's other recovery weeks. Exists purely to let the body absorb week 7's heavier two-quality-day load before the next build push.

weeks.label: Aug 25–30
weeks.bikeNote: Recovery week: daily bike is fine and beneficial. Helps move the legs without stressing them. No restrictions.
weeks.swimNote: Optional swim this week. If you're tired, skip it — rest is worth more than a pool session. Recovery week: if you do go, take the U-Bahn round-trip for work that day (save your legs).
weeks.tip: Second recovery week. Don't add km to compensate. The last 3 weeks have packed adaptation into your legs — let it consolidate.

training.title: Recovery run
training.detail: 40 min very slow (~65-75% LT) — mid-block recovery

days.movement: Bike both ways fine -- genuinely easy effort on a recovery week, nothing about the commute needs protecting.
days.food: Normal balanced meals, lighter carb share -- recovery week, not a loading day.
days.bigPicture: Week 8's recovery-pace run, deliberately very slow (~65-75% LT). Week 7 landed close to its original ~45km estimate (44.6km) -- Monday's medium-long got skipped, but Tuesday's LT-cruise intervals happened as scheduled, so the two roughly offset. CTL is climbing at a healthy +2.44/week, still under the safe ramp ceiling. Banking rest now is what makes week 9's build resumption land properly.

training.title: Swim (optional)
training.detail: Recovery week: 25 min of light swimming is fine, or skip if the body feels tired. Nothing forced.

days.movement: Bike both ways to the pool if you go -- this session is explicitly optional this week, skip without guilt if the body feels tired.
days.food: Normal balanced meals.
days.bigPicture: Recovery week's swim is optional by design -- light aerobic movement if it feels good, nothing forced. The week's job is rest, not another training stimulus.

training.title: Easy run + strides
training.detail: 45 min + 5×80m progressive

days.movement: Bike both ways fine -- easy effort plus a few strides, nothing that needs fresh legs for the commute.
days.food: Normal balanced meals -- recovery week, no special fueling needed.
days.bigPicture: Recovery week's next-to-last session: easy running with a handful of progressive strides to keep some sharpness without adding real fatigue, ahead of Saturday's reduced long run.

training.title: Reduced long run
training.detail: 75 min — active recovery

days.movement: No cycling -- Saturday, active-recovery long run, keep the whole morning easy.
days.food: Normal balanced meals with a moderate carb bump -- this is active recovery, not a hard effort, so no special carb-loading needed.
days.bigPicture: Week 8's reduced long run (75 min, active recovery) closes out the recovery week -- meaningfully shorter than week 7's 105-minute long run, letting the legs fully absorb the two-quality-day block before week 9 picks the build back up.

training.title: Sunday easy run
training.detail: ~41 min (~6.9 km), easy effort (~65-75% LT)

days.movement: No commute today, it's the weekend -- nothing to plan around for this easy run.
days.food: Normal balanced meals.
days.bigPicture: First day of week 9, back into build-phase loading after week 8's recovery week. A short easy run (~41 min) to open the week gently before Monday's medium-long run and Tuesday/Thursday's two quality sessions resume. VO2max ticked up to 59 (from 58) on the last update -- a good sign the aerobic fitness is still building even while LT itself (167bpm, ~4:57/km) holds steady.

weeks.label: Aug 31–Sep 6
weeks.bikeNote: Monday's medium-long and Tuesday's LT intervals: bike both ways is fine if legs feel fresh, U-Bahn if heavy. Thursday: hardest session of the block. U-Bahn both ways — don't add 4.5km on already-stressed muscles. Friday: U-Bahn — save legs for the 110 min long run.
weeks.swimNote: Wednesday in the pool before Thursday's hard intervals. Don't fatigue yourself — it's preparation, not training. With 20km on the bike Wednesday (work + pool), take the U-Bahn both ways Thursday — fresh legs for the 3×2km.
weeks.tip: The long run with 30 min at MP is the key session for sub-3h. You learn to run fast when already tired — exactly km 30–42. Tuesday's LT intervals are now at 5 reps — one more than two weeks ago, building the threshold side of that same sub-3h equation.

training.title: Medium-long run
training.detail: 50 min at easy effort (~75-85% LT)

days.movement: Bike both ways fine -- back into build-phase loading, this stays a genuinely easy medium-long effort.
days.food: Normal balanced day with slightly higher carbs -- build phase volume is climbing again after the recovery week.
days.bigPicture: Week 9's Monday medium-long run, the first real volume day of the build resumption. Sets up the rest of a busy week: Tuesday and Thursday's LT-cruise/MP tempo sessions and Saturday's first 'quality long run' with a marathon-pace finish.

training.title: LT cruise intervals
training.detail: 55 min: 10' wu + 5×5' at threshold pace (~95-100% LT) + 1' float recovery + 10' cd

days.movement: Bike both ways if legs feel fresh after Monday's medium-long, U-Bahn if not — protect Thursday's 3×2km either way.
days.food: Carb-focused breakfast. Post-session: protein + carbs within 30 min.
days.bigPicture: Back from recovery week — legs should feel surprisingly good, and this is where the second quality day steps up: 5×5' at threshold pace, one more rep than week 7. Last build block before Peak phase. Make every session count.

training.title: Open swim
training.detail: 35–40 min. This week add 6×50m fast at the end — simulates the effort you'll do in Thursday's intervals.

days.movement: Bike both ways to the pool is fine -- TSB's neutral (+0.28) and this is a light aerobic day.
days.food: Normal balanced meals; a bit of extra carbs at dinner ahead of tomorrow's harder race-pace intervals.
days.bigPicture: Week 9 of the build phase, wrapping up before peak starts Saturday. TSB's flat around neutral after a mixed two weeks (some sessions ran hotter than planned, a couple were skipped) -- today's swim primes the anaerobic system for tomorrow's race-pace intervals, the week's hardest session.

training.title: 2km repeats
training.detail: 60 min: 10' wu + 3×2km at 4:15–4:20/km + 2'30'' rec + cd — race section simulation

days.movement: Bike both ways -- legs are fresh enough off yesterday's easy swim to handle the ride plus the session.
days.food: Carb-heavy day ahead of the race-pace intervals; refuel with protein + carbs within 30 min after.
days.bigPicture: Thursday's race-pace simulation is this week's centerpiece -- 3x2km at goal marathon pace tests whether 4:15-4:20/km still feels sustainable under real fatigue. This closes out week 9 before Saturday launches the peak phase.

training.title: Long run with MP finish
training.detail: 110 min: first 80 at easy effort (~75-85% LT), last 30 at 4:20/km — first 'quality long run'

days.movement: No commute today, it's the weekend -- just get to wherever the run starts; no cycling before a long run with a fast finish.
days.food: High-carb dinner tonight and a carb-focused breakfast before the run -- this is the first 'quality' long run with race pace at the end, treat fueling like a dress rehearsal.
days.bigPicture: This is the first long run that blends easy volume with real race pace (last 30min at 4:20/km) -- a preview of marathon-pace-under-fatigue, and the last session of week 9 before peak phase begins tomorrow.

training.title: Sunday easy run
training.detail: ~25 min at recovery/easy effort (~65-75% LT) -- first finalized cut from the volume-escalation rule (update-coach.md Step 4f), applied 2026-08-17. Ramp headroom is thin this week (trailing CTL delta +2.17/wk against the conservative 3 pts/wk ceiling, since HRV/TSB have only been green 2 days running, not yet 'several'), so this is intentionally a small first cut -- expect it to grow on later runs as more headroom accumulates before this week actually starts.

days.movement: No commute today, it's the weekend -- easy shakeout, nothing structured needed.
days.food: Normal balanced meals; nothing special today.
days.bigPicture: First day of peak phase (week 10) -- this Sunday cut stays intentionally short per the volume-escalation rule (ramp headroom was thin when finalized), recovering from yesterday's first quality long run before the week's real load builds.

weeks.label: Sep 7–13
weeks.bikeNote: This week's schedule reshuffled: Wednesday's tempo and Friday's LT-cruise intervals are the two hard days -- U-Bahn both ways on both. Monday and Thursday stay easy-pace bike days. Saturday is full rest, Sunday's long run needs fresh legs, no cycling.
weeks.swimNote: No swim slot this week -- Wednesday's usual recovery swim became the moved-up long tempo instead.
weeks.tip: Peak phase: if you feel unusual pain, don't ignore it. One rest day now is worth 2 weeks of downtime later. This week reshuffled around a missed Tuesday session and a moved long run -- two real quality days (Wed tempo, Fri LT-cruise) plus Sunday's long run is still a full week. If anything feels off, dial back rather than pushing through all three.

training.title: Rest day
training.detail: Nothing done -- the medium-long run got pushed to Tuesday instead.

days.movement: Bike both ways fine -- an unplanned rest day, nothing to protect against.
days.food: Normal balanced meals -- no session today.
days.bigPicture: Ended up as a full rest day; the medium-long run originally scheduled here happened Tuesday instead.

training.title: Medium-long run (moved from Monday)
training.detail: 55 min at easy effort (~75-85% LT)

days.movement: U-Bahn both ways today -- picking up Monday's medium-long plus this week's accumulating load, worth protecting the legs from the extra commute miles.
days.food: Balanced meals with a slightly higher carb share -- peak-phase volume is building, worth fueling proactively.
days.bigPicture: Picks up Monday's medium-long run, run a day late (68 min actual vs 55 prescribed, steady 133-145bpm easy effort) -- Tuesday's own LT-cruise intervals moved to Friday to make room.

days.movement: U-Bahn both ways today -- protect the legs for this 40-minute near-MP block.
days.food: Best carb breakfast before the session. Recovery meal (protein + carbs) within 30 min after.
days.bigPicture: Takes over Thursday's originally-scheduled long tempo (40 min near marathon pace), moved up since Tuesday got used for Monday's medium-long instead. The rest of the week reshuffles around it: Thursday becomes an easy day, Friday picks up Tuesday's missed LT-cruise intervals, and Saturday's long run moves to Sunday.

training.title: Easy run
training.detail: 35 min at easy effort (~75-85% LT)

days.movement: Bike both ways fine -- absorbing yesterday's tempo, nothing to protect against today.
days.food: Normal balanced meals -- easy day between two real efforts (yesterday's tempo, Friday's LT-cruise).
days.bigPicture: Deliberately easy, sitting between yesterday's moved-up tempo and Friday's LT-cruise intervals -- a genuine recovery day in a week that's been reshuffled around this stretch of sessions.

training.title: LT cruise intervals
training.detail: 60 min: 10' wu + 4×6' at threshold pace (~95-100% LT) + 1' float recovery + 10' cd

days.movement: U-Bahn both ways -- protect the legs for the threshold intervals, especially two days after Wednesday's tempo.
days.food: Carb-focused day ahead of the threshold work; protein + carbs promptly after to start recovery before Sunday's long run.
days.bigPicture: Picks up Tuesday's LT-cruise intervals, moved here after Tuesday ended up being used for Monday's medium-long instead. Threshold work at 4x6' -- the week's other real quality stimulus alongside Wednesday's tempo.

training.title: Rest day
training.detail: Athlete's call: this week's long run moved to Sunday, freeing Saturday for full rest.

days.movement: No commute today, it's the weekend -- full rest, no cycling.
days.food: Normal balanced meals -- resting up for tomorrow's long run.
days.bigPicture: Rest day, freed up by moving the long run to Sunday -- a full day of recovery between Friday's intervals and Sunday's ~25km effort.

training.title: Long run (moved from Saturday)
training.detail: 150 min (~25 km), easy effort (~75-85% LT)

days.movement: No commute today, it's the weekend -- no cycling before this one, save the legs entirely for the ~25km long run.
days.food: High carb the night before and morning of -- bring fuel for a 150-minute effort. Recovery meal within 30 min after.
days.bigPicture: Takes over Saturday's long run, moved here after this week's reshuffle (Tuesday's LT-cruise -> Friday, Thursday's tempo -> Wednesday). This overrides the volume-escalation rule's earlier finalized 20-min recovery run for this slot. With the week boundary now correctly running Monday-Sunday, this Sunday is properly part of week 10, not week 11 -- so it doesn't stack on top of next week's own hardest-week schedule.

weeks.label: Sep 14–20
weeks.bikeNote: Hardest week of the plan. Monday: easy bike both ways for the medium-long run — held steady, not increased. Thursday: U-Bahn BOTH ways — the 3×3km needs completely fresh legs, no bike today.
weeks.swimNote: Wednesday between the hardest sessions. LIGHT swim — 30 min max, easy crawl. No extra efforts in the water this week. Hardest week of the plan: U-Bahn round-trip for work Wednesday, and separately bike round-trip to the pool (or do both round-trips the same way if you prefer) — don't do 20km today.
weeks.tip: 29 km is your training maximum this cycle — built up from a lower base than Higdon's classic plan on a shorter runway, but chosen deliberately to stay injury-safe. The marathon is completed through 15 weeks of work, not one single session.

training.title: Medium-long run
training.detail: 55 min at easy effort (~75-85% LT) — held steady, not increased

days.movement: Bike both ways fine -- moderate day, nothing to protect against yet.
days.food: Normal balanced meals with a solid carb base -- still building toward Thursday's hardest session of the plan.
days.bigPicture: Week 11's medium-long run, held steady at 55 minutes rather than increased -- deliberately kept moderate so Thursday's 3x3km threshold reps and Saturday's 29km peak long run get full legs.

training.title: Easy run
training.detail: 65 min

days.movement: Bike both ways fine.
days.food: Normal balanced meals, easy-effort day.
days.bigPicture: Deliberately plain-easy Tuesday this week -- week 11 is the hardest week of the plan, so the usual LT-cruise intervals are skipped here on purpose. A third quality day in the hardest week would be bad periodization even with good readiness.

training.title: Swim — active recovery
training.detail: 30–35 min light swim. Legs heavy from Tuesday? Water is your best friend today.

days.movement: Bike both ways to the pool is fine.
days.food: Normal balanced meals, light day.
days.bigPicture: Active-recovery swim between Tuesday's easy day and Thursday's hardest session of the plan -- a real break in the water before the week's biggest quality test.

training.title: 3km repeats
training.detail: 65 min: 10' wu + 3×3km at 4:15/km + 3' rec + cd — hardest session of the plan

days.movement: U-Bahn both ways -- this is the plan's hardest quality session, protect the legs coming and going.
days.food: Best carb breakfast. This is the biggest tempo stimulus in the whole plan -- fuel properly beforehand, and get a real recovery meal (protein + carbs) within 30 min after.
days.bigPicture: The hardest session of the entire plan -- 3x3km at 4:15/km, real race-pace-adjacent threshold work. This is what week 11 exists to deliver; Saturday's 29km peak long run two days later means recovery between the two matters as much as the session itself.

training.title: Peak long run
training.detail: 165 min (~29 km): first 145 min at easy effort (~75-85% LT), last 20 min at 4:20/km — your longest run ever

days.movement: No commute today, it's the weekend -- no cycling before this one. Your longest run ever (29km) -- get to the start rested.
days.food: High carb loading the day before and morning of. Bring fuel for a 165-minute effort -- the longest run of the entire plan. Recovery meal within 30 min after, this one will need it.
days.bigPicture: The plan's peak long run -- 165 minutes, ~29km, your longest run ever, capping the hardest week of the block. Everything since week 7's volume escalation has been building toward this session; next week (12) is a full recovery week to absorb it before the final push toward taper.

training.title: Sunday easy run (short)
training.detail: 20 min very easy (~65-75% LT) — recovery week, kept short rather than skipped

days.movement: No commute today, it's the weekend -- very short recovery jog only.
days.food: Normal balanced meals -- full recovery week starting, no need to overthink carbs today.
days.bigPicture: Week 12, a full recovery week right after the plan's hardest week and longest-ever run. This short 20-minute shakeout is intentional -- absorb, don't build, this week.

weeks.label: Sep 22–27
weeks.bikeNote: Post-peak recovery week: daily bike is fine and very beneficial. Helps keep circulation going and loosen legs after the 29 km.
weeks.swimNote: Wednesday: swimming as therapy. You can spend just 20 min in the water. The goal is to come out feeling lighter than when you went in. Post-peak recovery week: 20km on the bike today is ok — running load is reduced.
weeks.tip: Third recovery week. The body is consolidating the 29 km and 3km repeats. You may feel 'out of shape' — it's a feeling, not reality.

training.title: Recovery run
training.detail: 50 min very slow (~65-75% LT) — mandatory unload after peak week

days.movement: Bike both ways fine -- very easy effort day.
days.food: Normal balanced meals, nothing carb-loaded needed -- this is an unload week.
days.bigPicture: Still week 12's mandatory unload after week 11's peak effort. Slow and unhurried is the entire point of this session -- the fitness from the last two weeks needs to be absorbed, not chased.

training.title: Swim — unload
training.detail: 30 min relaxed swimming. Backstroke, floating, whatever feels good. Pure recovery.

days.movement: Bike both ways to the pool is fine.
days.food: Normal balanced meals.
days.bigPicture: Last easy day of the recovery week before Thursday's return to normal training -- pure recovery, nothing structured.

training.title: Easy run
training.detail: 50 min, free pace without watching the watch

days.movement: Bike both ways fine
days.food: Normal balanced day
days.bigPicture: Run without looking at your watch. This recovery week is for letting go — the hard work is done, now you consolidate.

training.title: Reduced long run
training.detail: 100 min — recovery from peak

days.movement: Easy bike before is fine this recovery week
days.food: Normal pre-run breakfast. Optional gel around 60 min if you want the practice — not essential for a 100 min recovery effort.
days.bigPicture: 100-minute recovery long run — a clear step down from week 11's 165-minute peak. Your body is storing the adaptations from peak week. You may feel 'flat' — that's normal and temporary.

training.title: Sunday easy run
training.detail: ~30 min (~4.8 km), easy effort (~65-75% LT) -- volume-escalation rule applied 2026-09-01: trailing CTL has been flat/slightly declining (-1.21/wk, well under the 3-5 CTL pts/wk ramp ceiling), so a modest addition was sustainable. Kept conservative (used the ~4 pt/wk midpoint, not the full 5) since HRV wasn't available this run to confirm 'green' status alongside TSB.

days.movement: No commute today, it's the weekend — exact plan for this day is still pending (see training note); no cycling before it regardless.
days.food: Normal balanced meals.
days.bigPicture: This week's Sunday easy run is governed by the volume-escalation rule rather than a fixed number decided in advance — its exact length will be set based on how CTL/TSB/HRV actually respond to the added volume in the preceding weeks, not guessed today.

weeks.label: Sep 28–Oct 3
weeks.bikeNote: Monday's medium-long and Tuesday's LT intervals: easy bike both ways is fine. Thursday (3×10' at 4:16/km): U-Bahn BOTH ways — this is the definitive proof you can run sub-3h, legs fresh at 100%. Friday: bike fine (4.5km one way). Saturday before long run: U-Bahn.
weeks.swimNote: Wednesday: last 'serious' swim session. From here on, swim only if you feel like it — taper starts in a few days. Thursday you have 3×10' at 4:16/km: don't do 20km on the bike Wednesday — U-Bahn round-trip for work, and separately bike round-trip to pool (11km).
weeks.tip: The 3×10' at exactly 4:16/km give you definitive proof: you have the fitness for sub-3h. From here, protect the work you've done.

training.title: Medium-long run
training.detail: 45 min at easy effort (~75-85% LT) — stepping back as taper approaches

days.movement: Easy bike both ways
days.food: Normal balanced day.
days.bigPicture: Final Monday medium-long run of the cycle, stepped back to 45 minutes. From here, every session is about protecting fitness, not adding to it — taper starts next week.

training.title: LT cruise intervals
training.detail: 60 min: 10' wu + 3×6' at threshold pace (~95-100% LT) + 1' float recovery + 10' cd — reduced reps, taper approaching

days.movement: Easy bike both ways
days.food: Carb-focused breakfast. Post-session: protein + carbs within 30 min.
days.bigPicture: Final LT session of the cycle — one rep fewer than two weeks ago, since taper starts right after this week. Final push before taper: three hard-ish sessions this week (Tuesday LT, Thursday's exact-pace 3×10', Saturday's long run), then the volume drops for good.

training.title: Swim — last serious session
training.detail: 35 min. Last time swimming counts as training. After this, recovery only.

days.movement: U-Bahn round-trip for work, and separately bike round-trip to pool (11km). No 20km today before Thursday's race simulation.
days.food: Carb-load today and tomorrow — Thursday is your final proof session.
days.bigPicture: Last serious swim session. After today, pool is optional recovery only. Enjoy the routine — taper starts in days.

training.title: Final race simulation
training.detail: 55 min: 10' wu + 3×10' at 4:16/km (EXACT sub-3h pace) + cd — last hard session

days.movement: U-Bahn BOTH ways. No cycling at all. Fresh legs only.
days.food: Best carb breakfast of the week. This is your race rehearsal day.
days.bigPicture: 3×10' at exactly 4:16/km — the definitive fitness test. If you hit all three intervals, you have the fitness for sub-3h on October 11. After today, you protect what you've built.

training.title: Moderate long run
training.detail: 130 min (~22 km) at easy effort (~75-85% LT) — last real long run

days.movement: U-Bahn to your run start. No cycling before.
days.food: Pre-run carbs. Gel at 45 min and 90 min. Post-run: recovery meal.
days.bigPicture: Last real long run. 130 minutes at easy pace, ~22km — a meaningful last exposure before the volume drops for good. You've done the work. Protect it.

weeks.label: Oct 4–10
weeks.bikeNote: Tapering: easy bike fine Monday–Wednesday. Thursday (quality session): U-Bahn. Friday–Saturday: U-Bahn or walk — legs to preserve for Sunday.
weeks.swimNote: Wednesday swim optional — only if you feel good and not tired. 20 min of easy arm work is enough. Don't add water kilometers.
weeks.tip: Tapering: legs feel heavy or strange? That's normal — the body is 'loading up'. Eat well, sleep a lot, avoid standing for long periods.

training.title: Easy run
training.detail: 30 min, free pace — enjoy the lightness

days.movement: Easy bike both ways — taper week, legs should feel surprisingly light
days.food: Start increasing carb percentage this week. Pasta, rice, bread.
days.bigPicture: Taper week. Legs may feel unnaturally good or strangely flat — both are normal. Your body is loading up glycogen. Run easy and enjoy the reduced volume.

training.title: Swim (optional)
training.detail: 20–25 min light swim if you feel good. If you're tired, skip without guilt.

days.movement: Easy bike both ways — or skip cycling entirely, it's taper week
days.food: Carb-heavy day. Pasta for dinner.
days.bigPicture: Optional pool session. 20 minutes of easy arm movement is enough. If you're tired, skip it — the race is in 3 days.

training.title: Last quality session
training.detail: 35 min: 10' wu + 3×1km at 4:16/km + 90'' rec + cd — short but at race pace

days.movement: U-Bahn both ways today — save legs for Sunday.
days.food: Good carb breakfast. Start carbo-loading tonight — pasta, rice, potato. 8–10g carbs/kg today.
days.bigPicture: Final quality session before the race. 3×1km at 4:16/km — short, sharp, and confidence-building. These legs are ready. After today, rest.

training.title: Pre-race jog
training.detail: 15 min very easy — move the legs, don't tire them

days.movement: No cycling today or tomorrow. U-Bahn everywhere. Protect your legs completely.
days.food: Day –1: light but carb-rich dinner, nothing new. Porridge or toast with honey and banana tomorrow morning.
days.bigPicture: Pre-race jog. 15 minutes to shake out the legs and calm the nerves. Nothing more. Lay out your kit tonight. Sleep early. Tomorrow is race day.

weeks.label: Oct 11 — RACE
weeks.bikeNote: Saturday before race: U-Bahn or taxi. No bike. Sunday post-race: whatever gets you home — just don't run.
weeks.swimNote: No pool from Thursday onwards. Final recovery is rest, carbo-loading, and sleep only.
weeks.tip: Sub-3h strategy: do NOT start fast. The biggest predictor of a blown-up finish is starting too fast, not failing to speed up late — hold even pace and let that be enough. Control the ego at km 1–10.

training.title: MUNICH MARATHON — SUB 3H
training.detail: Start at 4:20/km for the first 5 km (even if it feels slow). Hold 4:16 to km 35. Then give everything. No bike, no pool today — just run.

days.movement: No bike. Get to the start by foot or public transport. After the race: whatever gets you home.
days.food: Race morning: porridge or toast with honey, banana + coffee 2–3h before. Gel every 5–6km from km 15. Celebrate after.
days.bigPicture: Race day. 15 weeks of work comes down to this. Start at 4:20/km even if it feels slow — it is slow, on purpose. The largest pacing datasets show even pace beats a fast start every time — most blown-up finishes trace to the first 10km, not a failure to close hard. Trust the training.
